entry.name: buffer~
entry.description: Use the buffer~ object as a buffer of memory in which samples are stored to be saved, edited, or referenced.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: The first argument is a name used by other objects to refer to theto access its contents.For information about using named objects in Max for Live, click.

arguments.name: filename
arguments.description: After theobject's name, you may type the name of an audio file to load when theis created.

arguments.name: duration
arguments.description: After the optional filename argument, a duration may be provided, in milliseconds, to set the size of the, which limits the amount of sound that will be stored in it. (A new duration can be specified as part of amessage, however.) If no duration is typed in, thehas no sample memory. It does not, however, limit the size of an audio file that can be read in.

arguments.name: channels
arguments.description: After the duration, an additional argument may be typed in to specify the number of audio channels to be stored in the. (This is to tellhow much memory to allocate initially; however, if an audio file with more channels is read in,will allocate more memory for the additional channels.) buffer~ may have an arbitrary number of channels, only limited by the amount of RAM available. By default,has one channel.

messages.name: (drag)
messages.digest: Drag from the File Browser to load an audio file
messages.description: When an audio file is dragged from the Max File Browser to aobject, the file will be loaded.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.digest: Open a file buffer display window
messages.description: Double-clicking onopens a display window where you can view the contents of the. When the user clicks or drags with the mouse in theobject's editing window, the cursor's time location in the, in milliseconds, is sent out the outlet.

messages.name: (remote)
messages.digest: Alter or play back the loaded buffer
messages.description: The contents ofcan be altered by theandobjects or referenced/played-back by the,,,,,, andobjects.

messages.name: apply
messages.digest: Apply a function to a buffer's contents
messages.description: The word, followed by list consisting of one to three symbols or numbers, will apply a windowing function to the current contents of a.The word, followed by a single symbol that designates a windowing function, will apply that function to the current contents of the. Supported functions include triangle, hamming, hanning, blackman, welch, and kaiser. An additional second symbol argument of(e.g.) will calculate the function and apply only the second half to the whole.Note: The kaiser function requires a second floating point argument that specifies the beta parameter and precedes an optionalargument (e.g.).The word, followed by the wordand a floating-point number that specifies a gain value, will scale every sample by the gain coefficient.and a floating-point number that specifies a constant value that will be added to every sample in the buffer~.The word, followed by the word, will replace every sample value with the a new value representing the difference from the previous sample.

messages.name: bang
messages.digest: Redraw the waveform display window
messages.description: Redraws the contents of theobject's waveform display window. You can open the display window by double-clicking on theobject.

messages.name: clear
messages.digest: Erase the contents of the
messages.description: Erases the contents of.

messages.name: clearlow
messages.digest: Erase the contents of theas a low-priority task
messages.description: Erases the contents of the buffer like themessage, but performs the clear as a low-priority task.

messages.name: crop
messages.digest: Trim thecontents to new start and end points
messages.description: Themessage, followed by two numbers that specify start and end time in milliseconds, will trim the audio data in the buffer. It resizes the buffer~ to the selection length.

messages.name: duplicate
messages.digest: Import the contents of another
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies the name of a, will import the contents of the named buffer.

messages.name: enumerate
messages.digest: Post messages identifying allobjects which reference the same data
messages.description: Posts information in the Max Console identifying allobjects which reference the same data stored in theobject which received themessage.(The labelling information: "(this one)", will appear next to the address of theobject which received themessage).

messages.name: fill
messages.digest: Fill aobject with a constant or a mathematical function
messages.description: The word, followed by list consisting of one to three symbols or numbers, specifies how the contents of aobject will be filled.The word, followed by a single floating-point number, will set every sample in theto that value.The word, followed by a symbol that designates a function, will fill thewith one cycle of that function. Supported functions include sin (sine), cos, (cosine), and sinc. An optional second argument (e.g.) can be used to define the number of cycles of the function used to fill the. An additional optional third argument defines a rational number of cycles with which to fill the(e.g.will fill awith a quarter cycle of the cosine function).Note: the sinc function requires twoarguments that specify the number of zero crossings and an additional flag that toggles starting the function at zero (e.g.).

messages.name: import
messages.digest: Import a file
messages.description: The word, followed by a filename, reads that file intoimmediately if it exists in Max's search path without opening the Open Document dialog box. Without a filename, import brings up an Open Document dialog box allowing you to choose a file. The imported file retains the sampling rate and word size of the original file, but looping points and markers are not imported. The filename may be followed by a float indicating a starting time in the file, in milliseconds, to begin reading. (The beginning of the file is 0.)The starting time may be followed by a second argument - a floating point value that specifies the duration of sound, in milliseconds, to be read into. This duration overrides the current size of the object's sample memory. If the duration is specified by a negative value,reads in the entire file and resizes its sample memory and adjusts the number of channels in the file accordingly.The duration may be followed by a third argument that specifies the number of channels to be read in. If the number of channels is not specified (i.e., if the message includes only offset and duration information),reads in the number of channels indicated in the header of the audio file.If only two arguments are specified,imports the number of channels indicated in the header of the audio file. If three arguments are specified,imports the number of channels specified by the third argument. If the third argument is 0,imports the number of channels indicated in the header of the audio file.

messages.name: importreplace
messages.digest: Import a file with automatic resizing
messages.description: The word, followed by a filename, reads that file intoimmediately if it exists in Max's search path without opening the Open Document dialog box. Without a filename, import brings up an Open Document dialog box allowing you to choose a file. The imported file retains the sampling rate and word size of the original file, but looping points and markers are not imported. Theis functionally identical to themessage, except that imports are performed with automatic duration and channel resizing enabled by default. Unless otherwise specified, the duration and channel count of the imported file will be used to resize the buffer's internal sample memory.

messages.name: name
messages.digest: Change theobject name
messages.description: The word, followed by a, changes the name by which other objects such as,,,,,, andcan refer to the. Objects that were referring to theunder its old name lose their connection to it. Everyobject should be given a unique name; if you give aobject a name that already belongs to another, that name will no longer be associated with thethat first had it.

messages.name: normalize
messages.digest: Normalize thecontents
messages.description: The word, followed by a floating point number, will scale the sample values in theobject so that the highest peak matches the value given by the argument. This can cause either amplification or attenuation of the audio, but in either case, every value is scaled.

messages.name: open
messages.digest: Open thedisplay window
messages.description: Opens thesample display window or brings it to the front if it is already open.

messages.name: printmodtime
messages.digest: Post information aboutdata modification
messages.description: Posts information in the Max Console about when thewas last modified (i.e. written into, or modified in attributes).

messages.name: read
messages.digest: Read an AIFF/Next/Sun/WAV file
messages.description: Reads an AIFF, Next/Sun, or WAV file into the sample memory of the. The word, followed by a filename, reads that file intoimmediately if it exists in Max's search path without opening the Open Document dialog box. Without a filename,brings up an Open Document dialog box allowing you to choose a file. The imported file retains the sampling rate and word size of the original file, but looping points and markers are not imported. The filename may be followed by a float indicating a starting time in the file, in milliseconds, to begin reading. (The beginning of the file is 0.)The starting time may be followed by a second argument - a floating point value that specifies the duration of sound, in milliseconds, to be read into. This duration does not override the current size of the object's sample memory. It clears the current buffer~ data, then fills the requested amount at the beginning of the buffer~. However, if the duration is specified by a negative value,reads in the entire file and resizes its sample memory.The duration may be followed by a third integer argument that specifies the number of channels to be read in.If only two arguments are specified,reads in only the number of channels that thecurrently has. If the audio file has more channels than thecurrently has, the audio from all channels will be summed. If three arguments are specified,reads the number of channels specified by the third argument. If the third argument is 0,reads in the number of channels indicated in the header of the audio file.

messages.name: readagain
messages.digest: Re-read the most recently loaded file
messages.description: Reads sound data from the most recently loaded file (specified in a previousormessage).

messages.name: readraw
messages.digest: Reads the contents of an arbitrary file on disk, interpreting the data as audio into theobject.
messages.description: Reads the contents of an arbitrary file on disk, interpreting the data as audio into theobject. The arguments determine howinterprets the data in the file.The optional arguments are:
messages.argPattern: filename:symbol?, sample-rate:float?, channels:int?, format:symbol?, byte-offset:int?, duration-in-frames:int?, little-endian-flag:int?

messages.name: replace
messages.digest: Read an AIFF/Next/Sun/WAV file and resize the buffer
messages.description: Themessage is equivalent to themessage with a negative duration argument.

messages.name: samptype
messages.digest: Set the sample type to use when interpreting audio sample data
messages.description: In left inlet: The word, followed by a symbol, specifies the sample type to use when interpreting an audio file's sample data (thus overriding the audio file's actual sample type). This is sometimes called "header munging."The following types of sample data are supported:- 8-bit integer- 16-bit integer- 24-bit integer- 32-bit integer- 32-bit floating-point- 64-bit floating-point- 8-bit "mu"-law encoding- 8-bit a-law encoding

messages.name: set
messages.digest: Set theobject name
messages.description: The word, followed by a, changes the name by which other objects such as,,,,,, andcan refer to the. Objects that were referring to theunder its old name lose their connection to it. Everyobject should be given a unique name; if you give aobject a name that already belongs to another, that name will no longer be associated with thethat first had it.

messages.name: setsize
messages.digest: Set buffer length in milliseconds
messages.description: Sets the length of the sample memory of the buffer in milliseconds. Optional second argument sets the number of channels in the buffer. This limits the amount of data that can be stored, unless this size limitation is overridden by a replace message or a duration argument in a read message.

messages.name: sizeinsamps
messages.digest: Set the size of theobject's sample memory
messages.description: The word, followed by a duration in samples, sets the size of theobject's sample memory. This limits the amount of data that can be stored, unless this size limitation is overridden by amessage or a duration argument in amessage.

messages.name: wclose
messages.digest: Close thedisplay window
messages.description: Closes thesample display window if it is open.

messages.name: write
messages.digest: Write the contents ofto an audio file
messages.description: Saves the contents ofinto an audio file. A standard file dialog is opened for naming the file unless the wordis followed by a symbol, in which case the file is saved in the current default folder, using the symbol as the filename. Unless you change the format with the Format pop-up menu in the standard Save As dialog box, the file will be saved in the format specified by theattribute, or the file type of the most recently opened audio file. By default,saves in AIFF format.

messages.name: writeaiff
messages.digest: Write the contents ofas an AIFF file
messages.description: Saves the contents of theas an AIFF file. A standard Save As dialog is opened for naming the file unless the wordis followed by a symbol, in which case the file is saved in the current default folder, using the symbol as the filename.

messages.name: writeflac
messages.digest: Write the contents ofas a FLAC file
messages.description: Saves the contents of theinto a FLAC file. A standard Save As dialog is opened for naming the file unless the wordis followed by a symbol, in which case the file is saved in the current default folder, using the symbol as the filename.

messages.name: writeraw
messages.digest: Write the contents ofas a raw file with no header
messages.description: Saves the contents of theas a raw file with no header. The default sample format is 16-bit, but the output sample format can be set with themessage. A standard Save As dialog is opened for naming the file unless the wordis followed by a symbol, in which case the file is saved in the current default folder, using the symbol as the filename.The optional arguments are:

messages.name: writewave
messages.digest: Write the contents ofas a WAV file
messages.description: Saves the contents of theinto a WAV file. A standard Save As dialog is opened for naming the file unless the wordis followed by a symbol, in which case the file is saved in the current default folder, using the symbol as the filename.
